> **What this case shows** — the [transfer-entropy case](../te-cardioresp-bidmc/index.qmd) measured
> the *directed* coupling of respiration and pulse. **Mutual information** measures the *undirected*,
> symmetric dependence: how much information the two signals share, capturing any (nonlinear)
> relationship. The ecosystem had directed TE, coherence, cross-correlation, and distance
> correlation — but no general mutual-information op. This case introduces a **newly-authored op**,
> `mutualInformation`. On real cardiorespiratory signals it reproduces `sklearn.metrics.mutual_info_score`
> **bit-for-bit** (max |diff| ~**5e-16**), and it detects the coupling: the real RESP–PLETH mutual
> information (**0.077 nats**) is ~**3.2×** the histogram estimator's shuffled finite-sample floor
> (**0.024**) — the respiratory modulation the two signals share.

::: {.callout-tip title="The recipe you'll learn"}
**Workflow** — for the undirected shared information: `mutualInformation(x, y, bins)` → the MI in nats.
**Way of thinking** — mutual information is zero iff two signals are independent, and grows with *any*
(linear or nonlinear) dependence — it's the undirected sibling of transfer entropy (directed).
**Ecosystem usage** — `PhysioCrossModal::mutualInformation()`; pair it with `transferEntropy()`
(direction) and always compare against a shuffled control (the histogram estimator is positively
biased).
:::

## Proposition

On real cardiorespiratory signals (BIDMC-01), `mutualInformation` reproduces
`sklearn.metrics.mutual_info_score` bit-for-bit (max |diff| ~5e-16); and the real RESP–PLETH MI
(0.077 nats) is ~3.2× a shuffled floor (0.024).

## Question & goal

**The question is a gap and its fidelity: the ecosystem measured directed and frequency-domain
coupling but not the undirected shared information — can we author mutual information to reproduce the
reference, and does it detect the cardiorespiratory dependence above the estimator's bias?** The goal
is to introduce `mutualInformation`, certify it bit-for-bit against sklearn, and read the coupling.

## Challenge & approach

Histogram mutual information discretizes each signal into equal-width bins and computes
I = Σ p(x,y) log[p(x,y)/(p(x)p(y))] in nats — exactly `sklearn.metrics.mutual_info_score` on the
resulting bin labels. We implement that as `mutualInformation`, check it against sklearn on the
identical binning, and add a shuffled-surrogate control to expose the estimator's finite-sample bias.

```
RESP, PLETH (BIDMC, 25 Hz) → mutualInformation(bins = 16) → 0.077 nats
                    vs sklearn.metrics.mutual_info_score      → bit-exact (~5e-16)
                    vs shuffled surrogate                     → 0.024 (bias floor) → real is 3.2x
```

## Data

**BIDMC PPG and Respiration Dataset (PhysioNet)**: subject **bidmc01**, **respiration** + **PPG**
decimated 125 → 25 Hz, 200 s — the same git-tracked pair the
[transfer-entropy](../te-cardioresp-bidmc/index.qmd) and Granger cases use. Details in
[`artifacts/data_sources.json`](artifacts/data_sources.json).

The newly-authored op equals sklearn exactly, and the real coupling sits well above the estimator's
bias floor. Values trace to [`artifacts/mi_summary.csv`](artifacts/mi_summary.csv).

## Conclusion

`mutualInformation` fills a real gap — the ecosystem measured directed and frequency-domain coupling
but not the undirected shared information — and it is exact: bit-for-bit against
`sklearn.metrics.mutual_info_score`. On real cardiorespiratory signals it detects the undirected
dependence (the shared respiratory modulation) at 3.2× the estimator's shuffled floor, the
model-free *undirected* complement of the transfer-entropy fold on the same pair. The transferable
takeaway: **mutual information captures any (nonlinear) dependence between two signals; use it
alongside transfer entropy (for direction), and always compare the histogram estimate against a
shuffled control — it is positively biased, so the *ratio to the shuffled floor*, not the absolute
value, is the signal.**

## Open questions

- The histogram estimator is bin-count-dependent and positively biased; the **KSG/kNN** estimator
  (Kraskov 2004) is less biased and bin-free. Implementing a KSG `mutualInformation` — and a
  bias-corrected *effective* MI (real minus shuffled) across a cohort — would give an absolute,
  comparable dependence measure to pair with the directed transfer entropy. *Documented, not
  escalated.*

## Using this in your own analysis

| Step | Function | Package |
|---|---|---|
| mutual information (undirected dependence) | `mutualInformation()` | PhysioCrossModal |
| transfer entropy (directed coupling) | `transferEntropy()` | PhysioCrossModal |
| magnitude-squared coherence (frequency) | `coherence()` | PhysioCrossModal |

**Choosing the parameters.**

- **bins** — the number of equal-width bins per signal (here 16); more bins resolve finer structure
  but worsen the finite-sample bias, so pick with your sample size in mind.
- **the shuffled control** — always compute MI against a shuffled surrogate; the histogram estimator
  is positively biased, so the *excess* over the shuffled floor is the real dependence.
- **units** — the result is in nats (natural log), as in `sklearn.metrics.mutual_info_score`; divide
  by log(2) for bits.

**The recipe, copy-runnable:**

```r
library(PhysioCrossModal)

mi <- mutualInformation(resp, pleth, bins = 16)   # 0.077 nats
mi_shuf <- mutualInformation(resp, sample(pleth), bins = 16)  # ~0.024 (bias floor)
mi / mi_shuf   # 3.2x -- genuine undirected dependence above the estimator bias

# equals sklearn.metrics.mutual_info_score bit-for-bit (max |diff| ~5e-16) on the same binning.
```

**Auditing the numbers.** Every value on this page traces to
[`artifacts/mi_summary.csv`](artifacts/mi_summary.csv), and [`audit.py`](audit.py) re-checks the MI,
the bit-exact sklearn match, the shuffled-floor and ratio (and their internal consistency), and the
honestly-noted scope (newly-authored op; histogram bias; ratio-not-absolute; undirected complement of
transfer entropy).
